stemMd: According to the excerpt, the council bought the bell only after

options.label: A
options.textMd: the wool merchants withdrew their objection to the expense.

options.label: B
options.textMd: the weavers dropped their petition for a second bell.

options.label: C
options.textMd: the council had collected enough money from fines for lateness.

options.label: D
options.textMd: the fullers' guild was given the right to ring it.

options.label: E
options.textMd: the fullers' guild agreed to pay half of its cost.

explanationMd:
This is a stated question, and the signal words are in the stem: "only after". Scan the excerpt for that phrase. The second paragraph says: "the bell was bought only after the fullers agreed to pay half of its cost from their own funds." That is the choice about the fullers' guild paying half.

The wrong choices tempt by borrowing real details from elsewhere in the excerpt and attaching them to the wrong event. The merchants do appear, but as opponents of the expense. The weavers' petition is real, but it comes in 1441, after the 1437 purchase. The fines are real, but they were recorded in the twenty years after the bell was installed. Control of the bell is real, but it lay with the council, not the fullers.

**Check:** for each choice, name the sentence that supports it. Only one choice has a supporting sentence that also fits the timing and the people involved.

distractorRationale.a: The excerpt says the merchants "opposed the expense". Nothing says they withdrew that objection; the money came from the fullers.
distractorRationale.b: The weavers' petition is dated 1441, four years after the vote to buy the bell in 1437. It could not have been a condition of the purchase.
distractorRationale.c: This borrows the fines from the fourth paragraph. They were recorded in the twenty years after the bell was installed, so they could not have paid for it; half the cost came from the fullers' own funds.
distractorRationale.d: The bell was "in the council's keeping", which is what the weavers later complained about. The fullers were promised no such right in the text.

accessibilityText: A reading question about the accompanying excerpt on a town bell in Montalbero. It asks what, according to the text, had to happen before the council would buy the bell. Five answer choices; none uses notation or figures.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage states it directly: 'the bell was bought only after the fullers agreed to pay half of its cost from their own funds.' A is not stated. B is out of order, since the petition came later, in 1441. C is out of order too, since the fines came after the purchase. D is contradicted, because the bell stayed in the council's keeping. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tili-reading-logic-run6) reached the same answer: The text says directly: 'the bell was bought only after the fullers agreed to pay half of its cost'. A is not stated; the merchants opposed and were not said to withdraw. B, C and D are wrong on the timeline or unsupported; the council kept the rope.]

review.notes: Stated-information item keyed to the "only after" sentence. Each distractor reuses a genuine detail from the excerpt attached to the wrong event or the wrong date. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
